topic: Time response, stability and steady-state error
title: Step response of a first-order system
instructions:
## Reading a response curve

A heater is modelled as G(s) = 2 / (0.5s + 1). A unit step is applied at t = 0; the response is y(t) = 2(1 − e^(−2t)), which the plotter shows.

1. The time constant τ in seconds.
2. The final (steady-state) value.
3. The time at which the response reaches 63.2% of its final value.
4. The 2% settling time (use 4τ).

Now put a different plant, G(s) = 10 / (s + 1), in a unity-feedback loop with a unit step reference.

5. The steady-state error (use 1 / (1 + Kp) with Kp = G(0)).
6. The closed-loop pole.
hints: Write the denominator as τs + 1: τ = 0.5. The DC gain is the numerator, 2.
A first-order response reaches 63.2% at t = τ and 98% at t = 4τ.
